summary.oneLiner: Radico Khaitan delivered a milestone Q4FY26 with record 19% EBITDA margins driven by a richer portfolio mix and operating leverage, crossing INR 6,000cr revenue and INR 1,000cr EBITDA. The company is pivoting to a debt-free balance sheet by H1FY27 while guiding for 125bps margin expansion in FY27, underpinned by 20% volume growth in the Prestige & Above segment and aggressive luxury brand distribution.
summary.business: Radico Khaitan Limited (formerly Rampur Distillery & Chemicals Company), established in 1943, manufactures industrial alcohol, Indian Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL), country liquor and fertilizers, with IMFL as the core business. It has built its entire 20+ brand portfolio organically in-house across whisky, vodka, gin, brandy and rum, serving state governments, the Canteen Stores Department (CSD), private wholesalers/distributors/retailers, hotels/clubs/restaurants and international markets across 100+ countries.

Indian Single Malt: Rampur Indian Single Malt Jugalbandi #7 and #8
Vodka: Magic Moments Flavours of India (Alphonso Mango, Jamun SpicyMint, Thandai)
The Spirit of Kashmyr Luxury Vodka
Rum: 1965 Spirit of Victory Espresso Coffee Rum

endMarkets: Domestic India (30 states/UTs)|100+ international export markets|Canteen Stores Department (CSD) - defence institutional channel|Travel retail / duty-free channel

currentContext.strengths: Proven capability in building brands organically - entire brand portfolio developed in-house, among the few Indian companies to do so|Leadership across multiple IMFL categories with eight brands each selling over one million cases annually|Innovation-led product development and R&D driving continuous premium/luxury launches|Integrated manufacturing and supply chain network across own and third-party plants|Presence across 100+ countries providing wide global distribution reach|Strong and expanding premium and luxury portfolio supporting margin accretion|Experienced leadership and skilled workforce|Leading supplier of branded IMFL to the Canteen Stores Department (CSD), a segment with high entry barriers due to stringent brand registration requirements
currentContext.strategies: Drive value-led growth by scaling the premium and luxury portfolio|Strengthen leadership across key domestic markets|Expand presence in white spirits (vodka), leveraging Magic Moments' category leadership through flavours, premium variants and contemporary drinking occasions|Deepen international footprint, aiming to build globally respected Indian brands rather than merely export products|Expand travel retail presence (visibility, activations and advocacy across international airports)|Strengthen supply chain, capacity and backward integration - regional sourcing, PET manufacturing, glass bottle printing, malt maturation infrastructure and captive ENA capacity - to scale efficiently while maintaining quality and service reliability|Diversify into new luxury/lifestyle categories including tequila through the D'YAVOL partnership|Streamline corporate structure by merging Radico Spiritzs India and its seven wholly-owned step-down subsidiaries into the Company to achieve cost efficiencies and administrative simplification|Use digital planning tools, SAP-enabled systems and data-led procurement to improve forecasting, inventory management and supply-chain efficiency|The Company describes itself as firmly committed to shareholders through a consistent and shareholder-friendly dividend distribution policy; the Board has formalised a minimum 20% dividend payout policy while retaining flexibility to reinvest behind premiumisation, innovation and future growth. Alongside this, management has prioritised balance-sheet strengthening and debt reduction, stating the Company is on track to become debt-free in H1 FY2027.
currentContext.expansion: Radico Khaitan operates an integrated manufacturing platform of ten distilleries - six in Rampur (Uttar Pradesh), one in Sitapur (Uttar Pradesh), and three in Aurangabad (Maharashtra) held through a 36% joint venture - supported by a network of 42 bottling units nationally (5 company-owned, 6 under royalty agreements, 31 under tie-up/lease contracts). The Company has dedicated glass bottle printing units at three locations to support Magic Moments Vodka's growth and its own PET bottle manufacturing facilities in Uttarakhand and Telangana. During FY2026 the Company incorporated a new wholly-owned subsidiary, Radico Khaitan Scotland Limited, and made a strategic 47.5% investment in D'YAVOL Spirits (India and Netherlands entities) to build internationally relevant luxury spirits brands, including a potential entry into the tequila segment. A Scheme of Amalgamation to merge Radico Spiritzs India and its seven step-down subsidiaries into the Company is pending before the NCLT. The Company's stated strategic growth pillars include Capacity Integration, Indi-Lux and Luxury Expansion, Cost and Margin Discipline, Digital and Data-led Execution, International Business and Travel Retail, Consumer Experience and Brand Advocacy, and Innovation-led Portfolio Expansion.
currentContext.mdna: Premiumisation is the most important structural driver for the industry; Prestige & Above portfolio (now >45% of IMFL volumes, >70% of IMFL value) is the key growth and margin driver|Vodka and white spirits remain significantly underpenetrated versus global markets, offering substantial headroom; vodka also offers favourable category economics (shorter production cycle, lower working-capital intensity)|Margin expansion driven by three structural factors: premiumisation mix-shift, a supportive/benign raw material (grain, ENA) cost environment, and operating leverage as scale builds|Rising Indian consumption story - rising incomes, favourable demographics, urbanisation, digitalisation - supports long-term premiumisation and spirits demand|Progressive regulatory reforms in key states (Uttar Pradesh composite shops/digital licensing/e-lottery, Andhra Pradesh private retail participation, Karnataka rationalised duty framework) are improving ease of doing business, transparency and compliance, supporting industry formalisation|Cocktail culture, premium bars, casual dining and at-home social occasions are expanding consumption occasions and driving experimentation, particularly benefiting white spirits|Travel retail and duty-free channels are becoming more relevant as Indian outbound travel expands, increasing global brand exposure|Indian single malts and premium/luxury whiskies are strengthening credibility of Indian-made premium spirits and enabling them to compete with imported alternatives

risks.note: Ongoing global uncertainties, geopolitical tensions and moderating economic growth could dent consumer sentiment and discretionary spending; any slowdown in demand could hit IMFL volume growth and financial performance. Mitigated by a diversified portfolio across categories, price points and occasions, a premiumising mix, strong distribution and a robust balance sheet.

Volatility in prices of key raw materials - grain, ENA (Extra Neutral Alcohol), glass and packaging materials - plus potential supply-chain disruptions could raise production costs and pressure margins. Mitigated through a diversified supplier base, commodity monitoring, backward integration, regional sourcing and premiumisation-led pricing power.

The alcobev industry is highly regulated with state-specific laws, taxation, advertising restrictions and licensing; regulatory changes or compliance lapses could disrupt operations, delay product movement and hit profitability, as illustrated by policy developments in Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra. Mitigated by diversified geographic presence and a dedicated legal/compliance team.

Strong domestic and international interest in the Indian IMFL market, particularly in premium and luxury segments, could pressure market share and pricing. The Company relies on its brand portfolio, distribution network and high entry barriers to defend its position.

Evolving consumer preferences, rising health awareness and changing lifestyle choices - including a gradual shift towards moderation or alternative beverages - could structurally reduce demand for traditional alcoholic beverages over the long term.

Increasing environmental regulation, climate-related disruptions and sustainability expectations may affect operations, supply chains and resource availability (e.g. water, energy), requiring continued investment in energy efficiency and responsible sourcing.

As a consumer-facing business, performance is closely tied to brand reputation and consumer trust; product quality issues, regulatory non-compliance, negative publicity or inappropriate marketing could damage brand perception across a portfolio built almost entirely through organic brand investment.

one-line thesis: Radico Khaitan delivered a milestone Q4FY26 with record 19% EBITDA margins driven by a richer portfolio mix and operating leverage, crossing INR 6,000cr revenue and INR 1,000cr EBITDA. The company is pivoting to a debt-free balance sheet by H1FY27 while guiding for 125bps margin expansion in FY27, underpinned by 20% volume growth in the Prestige & Above segment and aggressive luxury brand distribution.
financial scorecard: Revenue: >INR 6,000cr (FY26), Q4 IMFL vol +4% YoY to 9.52mn cases; EBITDA Margin: 19% in Q4 (+565bps YoY), FY26 >INR 1,000cr; PAT: Not explicitly disclosed in transcript text but implied strong growth via ROE/ROCE improvement; Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Reduced by INR 329cr in FY26, targeting net-zero by H1FY27. One-offs: Q4 regular volume degrowth due to high base in AP (route change) and policy shifts in MH/KA.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Luxury portfolio +25% value growth in FY27; Prestige & Above volume +20% in FY27; Regular segment volume +3-5%; Margin: EBITDA margin expansion of 125bps in FY27 (inclusive of UK-India FTA benefits and cost pushes); Capex: INR 150-175cr focused on maintenance, efficiency, and optimization.
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Demand signals indicate strong traction in Luxury (INR 475cr sales value) and Prestige segments with 28% vol growth in P&A in Q4.
segment / subsidiary detail: Luxury: INR 475cr sales value, targeting 25% growth FY27 (Brands: Rampur 1943 Virasat, Spirit of Kashmyr, Jaisalmer). Prestige & Above: Vol +28% in Q4, +20% guided for FY27 (Brands: Royal Ranthambore +50%, Magic Moments +21% vol to 8.6mn cases, After Dark +60%). Regular: Vol degrowth in Q4 due to base effects/policy, but full year +30%; guided +3-5% vol FY27. Non-IMFL: Growing 7-8%, margin ~9% vs IMFL ~20-21%.
growth verticals / optionality: On-trade expansion (1,000 advocacy sessions planned); Geographic widening of luxury brands (from 10 to 20 states); Flavor innovations in Magic Moments (Flavours of India); Export market penetration (targeting 100 airports); Potential prohibition uplift in Bihar (wait-and-watch).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin 48% (+450bps YoY); EBITDA 19% (+565bps YoY). Drivers: Portfolio mix, operating leverage, price hikes (~60bps benefit). Risks: Glass prices up ~15% recently (factored in); Geopolitical tension in West Asia impacting supply chain; LPG dependency minimal (90% biofuel captive power).
capex / expansion: INR 150-175cr for FY27; primarily maintenance, efficiency improvements, and capacity optimization. No major greenfield expansions needed; 60-65% bottling outsourced via lease arrangements.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Deleveraging (target net-zero debt by H1FY27). Priority 2: Dividends (minimum 20% payout policy announced). Priority 3: Organic growth capex. Inorganic M&A ruled out currently unless ROCE >20-25%.
risks & watch-items: Regulatory policy changes (Karnataka pricing rationalization pending, Maharashtra MML stabilization, West Bengal govt change, Bihar prohibition status); Input cost volatility (glass, global crude/West Asia); Competition in MML segment in Maharashtra.
management quality / tone: Highly confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'inflection point', 'value-led growth', and 'financial prudence'. Clear focus on premiumisation as a structural margin driver rather than cyclical.
non-obvious takeaways: 90% of power/fuel at key plants (Sitapur, Rampur) is biofuel-driven, insulating against LPG crises. The company controls raw material procurement even for outsourced bottling units, mitigating supply chain hiccups. Magic Moments vodka volume (8.6mn cases) now rivals large global vodka brands in India, signaling a structural shift to white spirits among GenZ.
